newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev down about 18%, worst setback in day.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev down about 18%, worst setback in day.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev plummetted to a fresh low of 390-395 per dollar at the close of the interbank market from 330-335 in early trade after high foreign currency demand persisted amid very low supply, dealers said.
The 17-18 percent fall was the worst setback in a day for the battered national currency this year so far after it lost another 12 percent on Wednesday, closing at 330-335.
"The market was very nervous and confused and every dollar on offer was grasped irrespective of the exchange rate," a commercial bank dealer said.
However, dollar asks near 420 levs at noon did not meet demand, dealers said.
According to traders, trade was very thin in the afternoon as foreign currency supply was almost nil.
Traders said the central bank was not seen actively supporting the lev, although some dealers said it might have offered small volumes in early trade, dealers said.

Bulgarian National Bank's (BNB) governor Lyubomir Filipov said on Wednesday that the bank will continue to support the lev as much as it could but it could not deplete its reserves to counter a highly speculative dollar rush.

Filipov said this week's dollar-buying spree on the cash forex market was caused by "ill-intentioned" rumours that the finance ministry might suspend payments on treasury paper under a currency board system being discussed for Bulgaria.
The SSB, the country's largest savings institution, holds some 75 percent of its assets invested in government securities.

Individuals have withdrawn some 14 billion levs from the SSB since the middle of last week until Thursday, part of which were probably converted in foreign currency, SSB head Bistra Dimitrova told Reuters.
